purpose: Record verified semantic-lineage evidence for HeartFetter without assigning unresolved ConditionType=7 gameplay meaning. This unit tests whether exact enum-number continuity with the public 2018-10 client snapshot is a valid requirement for interpreting later HeartFetter conditions.

heroFetterSchema.finding: ConfigDataHeroFetterInfo contains GotSkills_ID as an explicit repeated skill-ID field.

battleInjection.finding: For each owned Fetter, the client indexes GotSkills_ID by fetter level minus one, resolves ConfigDataSkillInfo, and injects the resolved skills into BattleActorSetup.FetterSkillInfos.

buffConditionSchema.finding: ConfigDataBuffInfo contains explicit ConditionType and repeated ConditionParam fields.

findings: Official Langrisser Mobile update material for 2018-11-22 describes a second wave of heroes receiving 心之羁绊, proving the feature existed by that date.
Official Langrisser Mobile update material for 2018-12-06 adds 心之羁绊 to additional heroes.
historicalChronologyCrossValidation.implication: The public 2018-10-09 BuffConditionType snapshot predates the documented HeartFetter rollout window. Its observed enum range cannot be required to preserve the numeric value used by later HeartFetter condition records.

classSpecificPresentationCrossValidation.finding: Published HeartFetter Lv4/Lv7 reference pages present distinct effects under different final job/class names for the same hero, strongly supporting job/class-dependent HeartFetter presentation semantics.

preferred: A post-HeartFetter client protobuf/enum definition that names the relevant BuffConditionType semantic, regardless of numeric value continuity with the 2018-10 snapshot.
A post-HeartFetter runtime consumer that evaluates BuffInfo.ConditionType/ConditionParam against hero job/class state.
A version-linked ConfigData/client pair allowing the same HeartFetter skill/buff behavior to be traced across versions.

next: Continue ConditionType=7 semantic resolution using post-HeartFetter semantic lineage or runtime evidence. Do not require enum-number equality across client generations and do not create canonical job-restriction fields until the exact predicate is proven.
